summary: Read-only static delta review of the 9 changed files. All modified SQL statements checked textually: placeholder order matches bind order exactly, including growthAggregate's two identical subselects and readProvenanceChain's identity LIMIT 101 (both branches report identityLimitReached). EvidenceQueryScope.predicate is fully parameterized and its root '/' handling and normalization match MonitoringPolicy.includes/isIncluded. scopeHiddenCount correctly isolates the scope's effect from rootPath/category/modifiedBefore. Coverage downgrade logic never turns an honest 'partial' into 'none'. Two concrete defects found in the export path and the response-budget sizing; both are exercised by no existing test.

findings.claim: [P2] EvidenceBundleExporter applies its 25,000-row export cap to provenance_claims BEFORE Swift-side scope filtering, not after. A scope change can silently drop in-scope claims when out-of-scope claims consume the row budget first, and the cap limitation is derived from the post-filter count, so the truncation is never disclosed in exactly this case.
evidence: Sources/DiskStewardCore/Export/EvidenceBundle/EvidenceBundleExporter.swift:1104-1121 (readProvenanceChain: SQL has no scope clause, LIMIT applied first, Swift filter after)
Contrast: readEvents/readCurrentState/readCurrentStateAggregate/readSummaries push scope into SQL before LIMIT.
findings.recommendation: Push the scope predicate into the provenance_claims SQL before LIMIT, matching the pattern used for events/current-state/summaries; or compute the truncation flag from the pre-filter row count.

findings.claim: [P2] list_current_consumers' worstCaseItemBytes=1,536 undercounts the true worst case: currentItem serializes BOTH path and root_path through the same path_detail, so at path_detail=full with paths near PATH_MAX a single item can exceed 2,000 bytes, over-admitting rows into the pre-read clamp.
evidence: Sources/DiskStewardApp/IPC/AppEvidenceQueryBackend.swift:950-965 (currentItem shapes both path and root_path at the requested detail)
No test exercises path_detail=full with long paths.
findings.recommendation: Because the post-encode check still throws response_too_large rather than returning an oversized page this is not a leak, but legitimate full-detail requests over long paths fail more often than necessary and waste a read. Raise worstCaseItemBytes to account for two path fields, then add a test with path_detail=full and near-max-length paths.

evidence: Sources/DiskStewardCore/EvidenceStore/EvidenceQueryModels.swift:39-56 (EvidenceQueryScope.predicate: parameterized, root '/' handled as universal prefix)
Sources/DiskStewardCore/EvidenceStore/EvidenceStore.swift:2325-2356 (queryCurrentConsumers scopeHiddenCount computed against unscopedWhere including other filters)

coordinator_reconciliation.note: The reviewer listed the reviewed paths under changed_files; the reviewer changed nothing, so changed_files is recorded as empty here. Finding 1 fixed: readProvenanceChain and readCurrentProvenance now join the claim's event row and apply the scope predicate in SQL before LIMIT whenever a scope is set; without a scope the statements are unchanged. Finding 2 fixed: list_current_consumers uses a 2,688-byte worst-case item (two PATH_MAX strings plus fields); the post-encode ceiling remains the hard guard. A near-PATH_MAX full-detail fixture was not added; recorded as a boundary. Separately, the full-suite run of this snapshot exposed a time-base representation defect in retained-claim revalidation (see attribution-tolerance-*), fixed in ProvenanceEngine and ProvenanceChronology with a deterministic regression. Result remains advisory and candidate-bound; the corrected candidate is re-verified in full.
